obligations.expected_behavior: The public CLI and Python entry return structured result data for each invocation.
forbidden_result: An invocation returns an unstructured result or no structured result.
obligations.observable_result: Both the public CLI and the Python entry produce a structured result for the same invocation outcome.
obligations.state_after: A structured result is returned by the invoked public entry.
obligations.state_before: A caller invokes either the public CLI or the Python entry.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry
obligations.trigger: Any invocation of either public entry.

obligations.expected_behavior: The public CLI and Python entry use the contract's correct exit semantics for the invocation result.
forbidden_result: The exit status does not correspond to the contract-defined result semantics.
obligations.observable_result: The CLI process exit status and the Python entry's returned exit indication match the contract-defined success or failure semantics.
obligations.state_after: The invocation terminates with contract-correct exit semantics.
obligations.state_before: A public CLI or Python entry invocation is executing.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry
obligations.trigger: Completion of any public entry invocation.

obligations.expected_behavior: Diagnostics are returned as a bounded list whose diagnostic records expose rule, path, and message fields.
forbidden_result: A diagnostic record omits the rule, path, or message field.
obligations.observable_result: The structured result contains a bounded diagnostics list, and every diagnostic item has rule, path, and message values.
obligations.state_after: The result contains only a bounded, field-complete diagnostics list.
obligations.state_before: An invocation has produced zero or more diagnostics.
obligations.subject: Diagnostic result list

obligations.expected_behavior: Malformed JSON, an unreadable target, an out-of-root target, duplicate keys, and an unsupported contract version are all rejected as non-passing outcomes.
forbidden_result: An unsupported contract version returns pass.
obligations.observable_result: For each of the five invalid-input cases—malformed JSON, unreadable target, out-of-root target, duplicate keys, and unsupported contract version—the structured result is non-passing and the corresponding invocation uses failure semantics.
obligations.state_after: Each named invalid-input case is represented as a non-passing result.
obligations.state_before: The public entry receives malformed JSON, an unreadable target, an out-of-root target, duplicate keys, or an unsupported contract version.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry validation boundary
obligations.trigger: Processing any named malformed, unreadable, out-of-root, duplicate-key, or unsupported-version input.

obligations.expected_behavior: Two runs over identical input bytes under identical policy produce equivalent output in sorted form.
forbidden_result: Equivalent inputs and policy produce differing results.
The repeated output is not sorted as required by the contract.
obligations.observable_result: Running the public CLI or Python entry twice with identical bytes and policy yields equivalent sorted structured output.
obligations.state_after: Repeated identical runs yield equivalent sorted output.
obligations.state_before: The same input bytes and policy are available for two runs.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry output determinism
obligations.trigger: Two runs are performed with identical input bytes and policy.

forbidden_result: A timestamp appears in the returned structured result or diagnostics.
obligations.observable_result: Comparing the complete structured output shows no timestamp fields or timestamp values.
obligations.state_after: The returned structured output contains no timestamps.
obligations.state_before: A public entry has produced structured output.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry output
obligations.trigger: Returning structured results from either public entry.

forbidden_result: An environment secret appears in the returned structured result or diagnostics.
obligations.observable_result: The complete structured output contains no environment-secret values.
obligations.state_after: The returned structured output contains no environment secrets.
obligations.state_before: A public entry has produced structured output in an environment that may contain secrets.
obligations.subject: Public CLI and Python entry output
obligations.trigger: Returning structured results from either public entry.
